canonical_data: a working tree per task plus a local database of tasks, attempts, and execution processes
current_repo_note: Archived on the maintainer's own published declaration rather than a platform flag: the readme carries a sunsetting banner and the company behind it announced its closure in April 2026. Its final release retired the board and issue flows to an export-only page, so the product a reader would install no longer does what its name describes, though the per-task working-tree runs remain. No successor is named, so the supersession status does not apply.
strengths: Approval is real machinery rather than prose, with a service interface that creates a tool approval and blocks until it is answered
One adapter per vendor drives nine different coding-agent tools as supervised processes, each isolated in its own working tree
Substantial correctness infrastructure for its size, with hundreds of tests, dozens of schema migrations, and workflows covering the interface, the server, and the desktop build
weaknesses: The company behind it announced its closure, and the last commit, release, and package publication all fall in the same week of April 2026
Its final change retired the board and issue flows the product is named for, leaving an export page in their place
A promised community continuation was announced but no commit has followed in the months since
why_it_matters: Showed a task board as the surface for parallel agent work, with per-task working trees and blocking approvals, and then retired the board while the machinery beneath it stayed.
